high.title: Deposit Interest Rates May 2026: Broadly Declining
high.summary: Vietnamese banks have broadly reduced deposit interest rates in May 2026, with adjustments ranging from 0.2-0.8% across different terms and banks. State-owned banks show notable changes: Vietcombank now offers 3.5%/year for 6-9 month terms, 5.9%/year for 12 months, and 6.0%/year for 24+ months (its highest rate). BIDV maintains similar levels. This coordinated rate reduction reflects easing monetary conditions and reduced funding pressures across the banking system. For bond investors, lower deposit rates typically indicate declining yield expectations and potential capital rotation into government securities. FX traders should monitor whether this signals SBV's shift toward more accommodative policy, which could pressure VND if sustained while global rates remain elevated.

high.title: Proposed Amendment to Circular 22/2019/TT-NHNN: Adjusting Calculation of State Treasury Deposits in Safety Ratios
high.summary: SBV is considering revising Circular 22/2019 based on commercial bank requests to continue allowing partial inclusion of State Treasury deposits in mobilized funds rather than complete exclusion. The key change shifts from the "loan-to-deposit ratio" (LDR) to "credit-to-deposit ratio" (CDR), calculated based on total outstanding credit and total mobilized funds. This affects how banks manage liquidity and could influence their bond portfolio strategies. The revision maintains existing components including corporate bond investments and off-balance sheet commitments on the credit side, plus non-deposit funding sources. For government bond markets, any easing of these regulatory constraints could affect banks' investment appetite and portfolio allocation decisions.

medium.title: 20 Securities Companies Reported Losses in Q1/2026, with Losses Reaching 200 Billion VND
medium.summary: Twenty securities companies reported losses in Q1/2026, up from 13 in Q4/2025, reflecting challenging market conditions with insufficient liquidity breakthroughs and intensifying competition. EVS Securities recorded the largest loss at 197 billion VND. This indicates continued pressure on the brokerage industry amid limited market momentum.

medium.title: Group of Stocks Expected to Attract Strong Capital Flows After Holiday
medium.summary: Post-holiday market expected to show stronger differentiation rather than broad-based capital flows. Large-cap bluechips that led VN-Index gains may need a "rest period" after significant increases, while mid and small-cap stocks with stronger fundamentals could attract selective investment flows.

medium.title: "Identify" 7 Banks to Be Established in International Financial Center
medium.summary: Seven banks (Vietcombank, HDBank, SHB, MB, TPBank, LPBank, Nam A Bank) received shareholder approval to establish 100%-owned subsidiary banks at Vietnam International Financial Center with charter capital of 3 trillion VND each. This expansion could enhance Vietnam's financial market integration globally.

medium.title: Agribank Interest Rates Latest May 2026: Which Term Has Highest Rate?
medium.summary: Agribank maintains low deposit rates in May 2026 with maximum rate at 6%/year for long-term deposits. Rates remain unchanged: 0.2% for demand deposits, 2.6% for 1-2 months, 2.9% for 3-5 months, and 4.0% for 6-11 months, reflecting continued monetary easing stance.

medium.title: VN-Index Rises But Accounts Still Lose, What Should Investors Do?
medium.summary: VN-Index closed April at 1,854 points (+180 points), but many individual investors' portfolios remain negative due to concentrated gains in large-cap stocks while smaller stocks lagged. This "green index, red portfolio" phenomenon reflects strong market differentiation and selective capital flows.

medium.title: "Sell in May" Effect Really Scary for Vietnamese Stocks?
medium.summary: Historical data shows "Sell in May" effect is not prominent in Vietnamese stock market. VN-Index gained in May during 12 of the past 25 years (48% probability), but 70% probability in the last 10 years. The effect has weakened since COVID-19 as retail investors entered the market.

medium.title: Expert Names Two Important "Support Points" for Stock Market
medium.summary: May could be more challenging for stock market as short-term catalysts from AGMs and Q1 earnings are largely priced in. Analysts warn of technical correction risks given VN-Index gains were concentrated in few large-cap stocks while broader market participation remained limited.

medium.title: "Suffocating" Bank Lending
medium.summary: Rising interest rates creating significant burden for enterprises, especially production companies dependent on borrowed capital. Some companies report lending rates increased from 6-7% to nearly 9%, forcing postponement of green energy investment projects due to high financing costs amid oil price increases exceeding 100%.
